reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3, E4) supports the tribocatalytic activity, low friction, and wear performance of the (MoWNbTaV)_0.2S2 nanoflakes under high contact pressure when applied by spray coating on steel. However, no evidence is provided for the use of laser cladding, the bonding to TC4, the preservation of TC4's properties, or the feasibility of achieving the nanoflake morphology via this specific deposition method.
premises: Spray-assisted laser cladding can deposit a (MoWNbTaV)_0.2S2 2D HEA nanoflake coating on TC4 with strong bonding and minimal thermal degradation.
The (MoWNbTaV)_0.2S2 nanoflakes exhibit stress-triggered tribocatalytic activity under high contact pressures.
Tribocatalytic activity leads to in-situ formation of lubricious amorphous films that reduce friction and wear.
The coating can achieve low friction (COF ~0.076) and wear rates (~10^-9 mm³/(N·m)) under high contact pressures (~0.936 GPa).
The intervention preserves the beneficial mechanical properties of the TC4 substrate.
